boards.title: Your First Weekend at George Mason University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A flexible Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning the Fairfax campus, trying student spaces, and making a fare-free trip into Old Town Fairfax.

cards.title: Friday: Start with the Namesake
cards.subtitle: Meet at the George Mason Statue
cards.notes: Meet beside the seated bronze figure, inspect the Declaration of Rights and tricorne details, then take a clear group photo.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable outdoor landmark gives the weekend an easy starting point.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University’s history site identifies the Fairfax campus statue as a bronze work by Wendy M. Ross, unveiled in April 1996.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow posted campus access rules and avoid climbing on the sculpture.

cards.title: Friday: Learn the Campus Living Room
cards.subtitle: Get oriented inside the Johnson Center
cards.notes: Walk the atrium, locate the information desk and note one lounge or study room you can return to during your first week.
cards.short_summary: The central student center is a practical place to learn where everyday campus services live.
cards.evidence_claim: The Johnson Center contains lounges, study rooms, event spaces, dining, an information desk and other student services at 4477 Aquia Creek Lane.
cards.access_notes: Standard building hours are 7 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; individual tenants may keep different hours.

cards.title: Friday: Share the First Dinner
cards.subtitle: Compare meal-plan and door-payment options
cards.notes: Check the current menu before entering, agree on a meeting point inside, and use this meal to compare everyone’s weekend plans.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining-hall meal creates an unhurried first chance to coordinate with new classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason’s current catalog places Southside on the Fairfax campus and states that resident and optional meal plans are available for purchase.
cards.access_notes: Dining schedules can change by term or break; consult Mason Dining’s current menu and hours before going.

cards.title: Friday: Claim a Student Performance Ticket
cards.subtitle: Build the evening around the current arts calendar
cards.notes: Check the eligible-event list early, reserve through Mason360 when offered, and bring your valid Mason ID for ticket pickup.
cards.short_summary: A campus performance can anchor Friday night when student-ticket inventory is available.
cards.evidence_claim: Eligible students carrying paid credit hours may register for a limited quantity of free tickets to many in-person events, subject to availability.
cards.source_title: Free Tickets for Current Mason Students – Center for the Arts Event Calendar
cards.access_notes: Advance registration and same-day Mason ID pickup are required; confirm the event’s venue, time and ticket availability.

cards.title: Friday: Wind Down at the Hub
cards.subtitle: Use the student center as a late-evening base
cards.notes: End the night in a public lounge, scan the tenant directory, and note where Student Involvement and orientation staff are based.
cards.short_summary: A daily student center offers an indoor place to decompress without leaving campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hub is George Mason’s student-engagement center, with lounges, meeting spaces and student-service offices at 10423 Rivanna River Way.
cards.access_notes: The building’s standard hours are 7:30 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; tenants and paid attractions maintain separate schedules.

cards.title: Saturday: Find Your Study Base
cards.subtitle: Survey Fenwick before coursework accelerates
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, compare individual and collaborative areas, and save the full-hours calendar for later visits.
cards.short_summary: A low-pressure library walkthrough makes the first study session easier to plan.
cards.evidence_claim: Fenwick is the Fairfax campus’s main research library and includes research services, learning spaces, digital technology and group-study facilities.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s full-hours calendar before departure because daily and break schedules vary.

cards.title: Saturday: Test an Active Break
cards.subtitle: Explore the RAC’s recreation options
cards.notes: Bring your Mason ID, inspect the fitness and court areas, and ask the front desk which open-play option fits your access level.
cards.short_summary: A short facility tour turns campus recreation from an abstraction into a usable weekend option.
cards.evidence_claim: The RAC at 4350 Banister Creek Court includes fitness galleries, gymnasiums, basketball and volleyball courts, squash and racquetball courts.
cards.access_notes: Facility access depends on membership or pass eligibility; check current weekend hours and activity schedules before visiting.

cards.title: Sunday: Learn the Fare-Free City Link
cards.subtitle: Ride from George Mason toward Old Town Fairfax
cards.notes: Open the current route map, choose an Old Town stop, track the approaching bus, and note the return trip before boarding.
cards.short_summary: One practice ride teaches the public-transit connection between campus and central Fairfax.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fairfax states that CUE provides fare-free service connecting George Mason University with Old Town and other city destinations.
cards.source_title: CUE Bus | City of Fairfax, VA
cards.access_notes: Current service hours are Saturday 8 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; verify the route schedule and return departure.

cards.title: Sunday: Add Local Context
cards.subtitle: Spend an hour with the Fairfax story
cards.notes: Start with the permanent local-history gallery, pick up visitor information, and ask staff about one nearby historic site.
cards.short_summary: The city museum gives newcomers a compact introduction to the community surrounding campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fairfax identifies this site at 10209 Main Street as a museum and Virginia-certified visitor center with a local-history gallery.
cards.source_title: Fairfax Museum | City of Fairfax, VA
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Monday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed Tuesdays and listed holidays. Call ahead to check other closures.

cards.title: Sunday: Close Out in the Square
cards.subtitle: Pause in the center of Old Town Fairfax
cards.notes: Walk the garden and water-feature edges, review the city event board, and settle on your CUE return departure to campus.
cards.short_summary: A defined public square provides a simple final pause before the trip back to Mason.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Town Square is a City of Fairfax park beside Old Town Hall with gardens, a cascade water feature, event space and a splash pad.
cards.source_title: Old Town Square | City of Fairfax, VA
cards.access_notes: The directory lists daily dawn-to-dusk park hours; the splash pad and scheduled events have separate seasonal conditions.
